page: Microsoft Azure M128m is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 128 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 64 physical cores with 2.0 threads per core. The CPU operates at a base speed of 2.7 GHz and includes 38 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It is equipped with 3892.0 GB of system memory, providing 30.41 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage consists of a 14680 GB SSD, and there are zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core CPU, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded compression/decompression tests all scoring in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core and parallelized execution are robust. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark CPU score rank in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth is a primary strength, with uncached large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaching 382.78 GB/sec, placing it in the top 10% tier. Redis SET operations are also strong, achieving 80.7 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the M128m is its low single-threaded efficiency and poor text generation speeds during LLM inference, which falls into the bottom 10% for both 135M and 7B models. However, its high resource density, massive memory capacity, and large local SSD storage make it qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring vast memory footprints rather than high single-core clock speeds. This profile is suitable for large-scale in-memory databases, heavy database operations, multi-threaded data decompression, and static web serving throughput, which registered at a strong 55.93 GB/sec.
